title: PATHE: A Privacy-Preserving Database Pattern Search Platform with Homomorphic Encryption
problem: Database pattern search requires sensitive data handling, raising privacy concerns in centralized query systems.
motivation: Homomorphic encryption enables privacy-preserving database operations without exposing query data to the database server.
method: The system searches encrypted databases for patterns without decrypting them, using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (computation directly on encrypted data) combined with Hyperdimensional Computing (representing patterns as high-dimensional vectors for efficient matching). To make this practical, they built a hardware accelerator connected via CXL (a high-speed standard for connecting processors to accelerators) that performs both the encryption and pattern-matching calculations. They demonstrated it on protein spectra databases.
key_novelty: They created a hardware accelerator combining Fully Homomorphic Encryption (computation on encrypted data) and Hyperdimensional Computing (high-dimensional pattern matching) for private database searches.
contributions: FHE+HDC combined approach for encrypted search
limitations: Scalability to very large databases not addressed; communication overhead of encrypted queries not analyzed.
